nodes.What it is: A gripper is the tool at the end of an arm. Parallel jaws pinch, suction uses a pressure difference, and soft fingers bend around objects.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Match geometry and material to objects before adding learning; no universal gripper handles every surface. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: MIT manipulation course; industrial gripper designers

nodes.What it is: Contact forces and friction determine whether an object slips. Form closure blocks motion geometrically; force closure uses frictional contacts to resist disturbances.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Friction models help explain failures but uncertain surface properties limit predictions on hardware. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: Lynch and Park; MIT Robot Locomotion Group

nodes.What it is: A pick-and-place system finds an object, chooses a grasp, moves the arm, and releases it at a destination. Each stage must use consistent coordinates and recover when a grasp fails.
nodes.Prerequisites: Coordinate frames; basic inverse kinematics; gripper safety
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Reliable recovery and repeatable evaluation matter more than a single successful video. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

nodes.What it is: Teleoperation lets a person move an arm through a leader arm or another input device. Recording camera images and joint motion produces examples for imitation learning.
nodes.Prerequisites: Joint limits; calibration; timestamps; emergency stop
nodes.Frontier state 2026: The 2026 M3-Tele preprint studies synchronized multimodal demonstration collection and compliant whole-body teleoperation. Dataset quality, synchronized cameras and operator ergonomics constrain useful demonstrations; ALOHA 2 improves collection hardware. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

nodes.What it is: A grasp detector predicts where a gripper could hold an object from an image or point cloud. A good grasp score does not guarantee the arm can reach it without collisions.
nodes.Prerequisites: Point clouds; camera calibration; grasp mechanics
nodes.Frontier state 2026: GraspNet supplies a benchmark and Contact-GraspNet predicts 6D grasps; clutter, sensor gaps and execution remain limitations. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

nodes.What it is: Pose estimation finds an object position and orientation relative to a camera. The robot transforms that estimate into its own coordinates to approach the object.
nodes.Prerequisites: Rigid transforms; camera intrinsics; RGB-D data
nodes.Frontier state 2026: FoundationPose supports pose estimation and tracking; symmetry, occlusion and calibration still complicate grasp execution. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

nodes.What it is: Motion generation finds joint movements that avoid the table and other obstacles. It must check the arm links and attached objects, not just the gripper.
nodes.Prerequisites: Inverse kinematics; collision geometry; coordinate frames
nodes.Frontier state 2026: MoveIt 2 integrates planning and execution; cuRobo offers GPU-accelerated motion generation, with hardware and model requirements. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

nodes.What it is: Compliance makes an arm yield instead of pushing rigidly against an obstacle. Impedance control acts like a virtual spring and damper, useful when inserting a peg or following a surface.
nodes.Prerequisites: Dynamics; feedback control; force limits; contact mechanics
nodes.Frontier state 2026: M3-Tele (2026 preprint) explicitly combines contact-force feedback and tactile adaptation. Insertion needs contact-aware feedback and safe limits; a position-only hobby arm is not a torque-controlled research arm. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

nodes.What it is: Two arms can hold and manipulate an object together. Their motions must coordinate so they do not collide or pull against each other.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: DECO (ICML 2026) studies bimanual visual, proprioceptive and tactile policy conditioning. ALOHA 2 improves bimanual demonstration hardware; coordinated contact and robustness remain difficult. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

nodes.What it is: A mobile manipulator combines an arm with a moving base. The base must stop in a place from which the arm can safely reach and manipulate an object.
nodes.Prerequisites: Arm planning; base localization; safety zones
nodes.Frontier state 2026: M3-Tele (2026 preprint) extends whole-body teleoperation toward compliant contact-rich interaction. Mobile ALOHA demonstrates whole-body imitation; deployment in changing rooms still requires robust perception and recovery. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

nodes.What it is: Tactile sensors measure what happens where a finger touches an object. Camera-based gel sensors turn small surface deformations into images that can reveal contact and slip.
nodes.Prerequisites: Image processing; contact mechanics; sensor mounting
nodes.Frontier state 2026: DECO (ICML 2026) reports a tactile adapter for bimanual manipulation; results are task-specific, not universal touch robustness. Touch complements vision during occlusion; calibration, gel wear and generalization across objects remain challenges. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

nodes.What it is: Cloth and cables change shape while the robot moves them. Unlike a rigid block, they cannot be described by one position and orientation.
nodes.Prerequisites: Grasping; image processing; contact; learning basics
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Cloth Funnels uses dynamic actions to improve cloth configuration; generalizing across materials and folds remains difficult. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

nodes.What it is: In-hand manipulation changes an object pose while it stays between several fingers. The controller must repeatedly manage which fingers touch, roll or slide.
nodes.Prerequisites: Contact mechanics; multi-joint control; reinforcement learning
nodes.Frontier state 2026: STAR (2026 preprint) explores sparse tactile representations for dexterous vision-tactile-language-action policies. LEAP Hand makes research hardware more accessible; contact-rich sim-to-real transfer and reliable sensing remain bottlenecks. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

nodes.What it is: An arm can move objects by pushing, sliding or pivoting without holding them. These actions exploit contact with the table or a wall.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Contact mode changes make planning difficult; controlled pushing remains a useful complement to grasping. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

nodes.What it is: Task planning chooses steps such as opening a drawer before picking an item. Motion planning checks that each step can actually be executed by the arm.
nodes.Prerequisites: State machines; symbolic search; collision-free arm planning
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Combining symbolic choices with continuous geometry and recovery remains difficult; language plans need executable checks. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: MIT manipulation course; planning research community

nodes.What it is: Open-vocabulary systems accept descriptions beyond a fixed list of objects. Affordances describe useful actions, such as pulling a handle, rather than just recognizing its name.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: VoxPoser builds value maps and ReKep uses relational keypoint constraints; physical grounding and failure detection remain essential. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.

nodes.What it is: A vision-language-action model maps camera images and instructions to robot actions. Generalist policies aim to reuse experience across tasks, but still need the right action format and robot calibration.
nodes.Prerequisites: Imitation learning; datasets; arm interfaces; evaluation
nodes.Frontier state 2026: STAR (2026 preprint) adds touch to the vision-language-action recipe for dexterous manipulation. OpenVLA, Octo and pi0 demonstrate transferable policies; their published results do not guarantee reliable transfer to a low-cost arm. Scope note: this is a snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 SOTA ranking.
nodes.Key players: OpenVLA team; Octo team; Physical Intelligence

top3.justification: Best first win: very accessible simulated cube transfer, immediately understandable video, and a reusable manipulation stack for later demos. Zero incremental hardware cost in simulation; more relevance per euro than buying a dexterous hand first.

Strong bridge to the LeRobot ecosystem: leader-follower videos are clear and demonstrations feed later policies. Assembly is documented and hardware is simpler than a mobile or dual-arm platform, but current kit price is unknown; test actual data quality before committing the lab to this wedge.

High visual impact from grasp overlays and clutter clearing; public data and checkpoints let AI students contribute without building mechanisms. Offline work minimizes hardware cost and connects naturally to grasping research; real-arm integration is a separate risk.
